value.kid_phrase: Hidden courage — being brave even when scared

story_world: Ancient Persian Empire, city of Shushan (Susa). Ornate sandstone palace with Persian arches, mosaic tiles, carved stone columns. Lush palace gardens with date palms, pomegranate trees, flowing fountains. Desert climate — warm golden light, deep blue sky. Persian court aesthetic: flowing robes, turbans, ornate Persian-style crowns, rich textiles in golds, deep purples, and royal blues. Think Persepolis, NOT biblical Israel. Warm sandstone, polished marble floors, hanging tapestries, oil lamps. City streets have market stalls, stone buildings, Persian archways.

cards.image_prompt:
A magnificent golden crown resting on a plush royal purple velvet cushion with gold tassels at the corners.

The crown is ornate and detailed — delicate gold filigree with tiny purple amethyst gems set around the band. A subtle Star of David is woven into the metalwork, barely visible unless you LOOK for it (like a hidden secret!). The gold is warm and burnished, glowing from within.

A single dramatic beam of warm golden light streams down from above, illuminating ONLY the crown. Tiny golden dust motes and sparkles float in the light beam around the crown.

The cushion floats in a sea of soft, warm darkness. No walls, no ceiling, no hard edges — just the crown in its spotlight. A faint blue curtain edge and the silhouette of a column are barely visible at the far left and right edges, but they fade into shadow. Nothing creates a horizontal line across the image.

The ENTIRE upper portion of the frame is a seamless warm gradient — deep royal purple at the very top fading smoothly to rich amber around the light beam. Stars and tiny sparkles scattered throughout. NO ceiling, NO wall edge, NO hard lines. Just endless atmospheric glow above the crown.

WONDER AND MYSTERY — whose crown is this? What secret does it hold? A magical, hushed moment — like finding treasure in the dark.

back.say: **Today we're going to hear an amazing story. It's about a queen named Esther who had a BIG secret. She was Jewish — just like us! — but nobody knew. When her people needed help, she had to be SO brave. Let's find out what happened!**

ask.text: What do you think a queen's secret could be?
When have you had a really big feeling inside?

back.transition: Now let's meet the characters in our story!

guide.tip: Have children close their eyes while you describe the crown. It builds anticipation.

cards.image_prompt:
ESTHER:
Young Jewish woman, warm olive skin, large kind brown eyes.
Long dark wavy hair with elegant modest head covering.
Royal purple dress with ornate gold and blue embroidery at the neckline and cuffs.
Simple gold tiara with small jewels. Delicate gold earrings.
Hands clasped gently in front of her, one hand near her heart.
Gentle, brave expression — a quiet smile that hides a secret.

Esther portrait framed from chest up, face centered.
Behind her: a grand Persian palace archway with intricate geometric patterns.
Rich blue curtain draped to one side. Ornate gold columns frame the arch.
Warm golden light from the right illuminating her face.
The archway opens to a deeper palace room glowing with amber light.
Dark shadow pooling in the lower-left.

Warm, regal, kind. She's someone children will INSTANTLY root for. A princess with a secret.

back.say: **This is Esther. She became the queen! But she had a secret — she was Jewish, and nobody in the palace knew. Esther was nervous about her secret. But guess what? When it really mattered, she was SO brave. She's our hero!**

ask.text: What do you notice about how Esther looks?
Have you ever kept something special about yourself quiet?

back.transition: Let's meet another important person in our story!

pshat.text: Esther was a young Jewish woman who became the queen. She kept her Jewish identity a secret. When her people needed help, she found her courage.

guide.tip: Ask children to show you a brave face, then a nervous face. Builds emotional vocabulary.

cards.image_prompt:
MORDECHAI:
Older Jewish man, warm brown skin, kind wise eyes with crow's feet.
Full gray-brown beard, dignified tall posture.
Jewish head covering (cloth wrap in cream/white).
Modest layered robes in earth tones — brown outer robe, cream inner garment, subtle blue scarf.
Hands clasped peacefully in front of him. Grandfatherly warmth.

Mordechai portrait framed from chest up, face centered.
Behind him: the great stone gate of Shushan with ornate blue tile border.
Through the archway: palm trees, domed buildings, and a warm market street visible in the distance.
Bright blue sky above the gate. Warm afternoon light.
Dark stone wall fading into shadow at the lower-left.

Wise, trustworthy, SOLID. Like a favorite grandfather who always knows the right thing to do.

back.say: **This is Mordechai. He's like a wise uncle or grandpa. He helped raise Esther and always knew what to do. Mordechai was very brave too — he wouldn't bow down to anyone except God. He helped Esther be brave!**

ask.text: Who in your life gives you good advice?
What makes someone wise?

back.transition: Our story is about to get really exciting!

pshat.text: Mordechai was Esther's older cousin. He raised her and always gave her good advice. He stood up for what was right, no matter what.

guide.tip: Connect to children's lives by asking who gives THEM good advice.

cards.image_prompt:
HAMAN:
Adult man with DARK POINTED GOATEE WITH CONNECTED MUSTACHE.
DISTINCTIVE THREE-CORNERED HAT (like hamantaschen pastry shape).
Pouty frustrated expression, furrowed brow, eyes narrowed with JEALOUSY (not rage).
Persian clothing in MUTED dusty purple and gray-brown vest over lighter tunic.
Arms crossed defensively. Shoulders slightly hunched.
Looking to the side with a jealous scowl — lip pushed out in a pout.

Haman portrait framed from chest up, face centered.
Behind him: a palace hallway with Persian arched windows.
Palm trees visible through the windows — soft, warm, NOT dark or scary.
The background is neutral and warm — muted golds and tans.
Muted, slightly desaturated colors throughout. NOT dark. NOT ominous.
Dark ground shadow at lower-left.

Jealous and pouty — like a kid who didn't get picked first. NOT SCARY. Kids should recognize the feeling, not be frightened.

back.say: **This is Haman. He worked for the king and wanted everyone to bow down to him. But Mordechai said no — he only bows to God. That made Haman feel SO jealous. His jealousy grew and grew... and he made a very bad choice. Have you ever felt jealous? It's okay to feel that way, but Haman didn't make good choices with his feelings.**

ask.text: What does it feel like inside when you are jealous?
What could Haman have done instead of making a bad choice?

back.transition: There's one more person we need to meet!

pshat.text: Haman worked for the king. He wanted everyone to bow down to him. When Mordechai wouldn't bow, Haman felt very jealous.

guide.extend: Sometimes when we feel jealous, we want to do something mean. But that's not a good choice. We can talk about our feelings instead.
guide.tip: Normalize the feeling of jealousy before discussing Haman's bad choice. Children need to know feelings are okay.

cards.image_prompt:
KING ACHASHVEROSH:
Adult man, somewhat cartoonish and comedic.
Large ornate Persian crown with red jewel — slightly too big, tilting on his head.
Fancy royal robes in rich reds and golds with blue sash.
Big bushy dark beard, wide bewildered eyes, eyebrows raised high.
One hand scratching his head under the crown. Other hand on his hip.
Expression: confused, distracted — "Wait, what's going on?"

King portrait framed from chest up, face centered.
Behind him: the ornate Persian throne room — same architectural style as Esther's spotlight.
Colorful geometric mosaic tiles on the walls. Ornate Persian arched doorway.
Rich warm light from above. Jeweled decorations glinting.
Dark throne room shadow at lower-left.

Bumbling, confused, slightly SILLY — but not mean. A king who needs help thinking things through. Kids will giggle at him!

back.say: **This is King Achashverosh. He was the king! But you know what? He didn't always stop to think. When Haman told him a bad plan, the king just said yes without asking questions. That wasn't smart! We should always think first and ask questions. But don't worry — the king learns his lesson!**

ask.text: Why is it important to ask questions before deciding?
What happens when you say yes too fast without thinking?

back.transition: Now let's see how our story begins!

pshat.text: King Achashverosh ruled a very big kingdom. He didn't always think before he decided things. He listened to Haman without asking enough questions.

guide.extend: It's important to think before we decide. We should ask questions and not just say yes right away.
guide.tip: Use a silly voice for the king to keep the mood light and age-appropriate.

cards.image_prompt:
ESTHER:
Young Jewish woman, warm olive skin, large kind brown eyes.
Long dark hair with elegant modest head covering.
Royal purple and blue flowing dress, simple gold tiara.

Esther seated on a cushioned bench in the palace throne room.
King Achashverosh standing beside her, gently placing a golden crown on her head.
Esther looks up with wide nervous eyes — her hands clasped in her lap.
She's beautiful but overwhelmed. This is the biggest moment of her life!
Palace courtiers visible in background, watching the ceremony.
Warm golden light streaming through tall Persian arched windows.
Ornate mosaic tiles on the walls, rich tapestries hanging, oil lamps glowing.
High vaulted ceiling fading into warm amber haze above.
Dark polished marble floor with shadow pooling in the lower-left.

Magical, exciting, but with a hint of nervousness. A fairy-tale moment with a secret underneath.

back.say: **The king needed a new queen, and he chose Esther! She was so beautiful and kind. She moved into the big palace and wore a shiny crown. But Esther had a secret — shhh! — she didn't tell anyone she was Jewish. Let's all put on our pretend crowns and wave like Queen Esther!** [Put an imaginary crown on your head and give a royal wave!]

ask.text: How would it feel to live in a beautiful palace?
What would be hard about keeping a really big secret?

back.transition: Let's find out what happens next!

pshat.text: The king chose Esther to be his new queen. She moved into the beautiful palace. But she kept her secret — she didn't tell anyone she was Jewish.

guide.tip: Whisper 'shhh' when you mention the secret — children love the dramatic effect.

cards.image_prompt:
MORDECHAI:
Older Jewish man, warm brown skin, kind wise eyes.
Full gray-brown beard. Wrapped cloth turban on his head.
Modest robes in earth tones. Standing TALL, arms at his sides, chin up, shaking his head NO.

HAMAN:
Adult man with DARK POINTED GOATEE WITH CONNECTED MUSTACHE.
DISTINCTIVE THREE-CORNERED HAT (like hamantaschen pastry shape).
Pouty frustrated expression, pointing angrily at Mordechai.
Muted dusty purple and gray-brown clothing.

Outside the palace gates in Shushan — ornate Persian archways, warm sandstone.
Haman stands by the gate on the left. A crowd of people kneeling and bowing before him.
Mordechai stands on the right, the ONLY one not bowing — tall, dignified, refusing.
Haman points at Mordechai, furious that he won't bow.

back.say: **Haman walked through the streets and wanted everyone to bow down to him. But when he passed Mordechai, guess what happened? Mordechai stood up TALL. He shook his head and said NO! Mordechai only bows to God. Let's all stand up tall like Mordechai! Stand straight... now shake your head NO!** [Stand up straight and tall! Shake your head NO!]

ask.text: Have you ever said no to something you thought was wrong?
What makes Mordechai's choice so brave?

back.transition: Uh oh — something's about to go wrong...

pshat.text: Haman wanted everyone to bow down to him. But Mordechai said no! He stood tall and would not bow.

guide.tip: Let every child stand up for this one. The physical movement helps them remember the lesson.

cards.image_prompt:
Haman — THREE-CORNERED HAT (hamantaschen shape), dark pointed goatee, dusty purple and gray-brown robes — sitting hunched on a cushion, arms crossed tight, pouty frustrated frown. NOT scary, just jealous and sulky like a child who didn't get their way.

A LARGE thought bubble to the RIGHT of Haman, positioned LOW — at chest/belly height, in the CENTER-RIGHT of the frame. NOT near the top of the image. Inside the thought bubble: Mordechai standing tall with arms at his sides, refusing to bow. The thought bubble should be prominent. The entire TOP 30% of the frame must be EMPTY — just wall, ceiling, or atmospheric space.

Crumpled papers and a scroll on the floor. Simple stone room, single arched window. Warm dim light — gloomy but not scary.
Dark floor and shadow in the lower-left corner.

back.say: **Uh oh. Haman was SO jealous and angry that Mordechai wouldn't bow. His jealousy grew and grew until he made a VERY bad choice. He decided he wanted to hurt all the Jewish people! That was SO wrong. Can you make a jealous, pouty face like Haman? Cross your arms... Now — is that a good choice? NO! Haman needed to stop and think.** [Make a jealous, pouty face and cross your arms!]

ask.text: What could Haman have done with his jealous feelings instead?
How can we stop ourselves from making bad choices when we're upset?

back.transition: But don't worry — someone is about to be very brave!

pshat.text: Haman felt SO jealous that Mordechai wouldn't bow. His jealousy grew bigger and bigger. He made a plan to hurt all the Jewish people. That was wrong!

guide.tip: Pause after 'Is that a good choice?' and let children shout 'NO!' together.

cards.image_prompt:
A grand banquet scene in the palace.
Esther stands center, pointing directly at Haman. Her left hand pressed over her heart.
She is REVEALING the truth — "This is the man!"

King Achashverosh on his throne to the left, leaning forward with shock.
Haman on the right, shrinking back in terror, hands up defensively.

A banquet table with goblets and platters in the foreground.
Ornate Persian columns and rich tapestries on the walls.

back.say: **Mordechai ran to tell Esther about Haman's terrible plan. Esther was scared — really scared! But she knew she had to help. She took a deep breath and went to see the king. Then she said the bravest words: 'I have something important to tell you. I am Jewish!' Let's practice being brave like Esther. Take a deep breath... now say 'I have something important to tell you!'** [Take a deep breath and say 'I have something important to tell you!']

ask.text: What gives you courage when you need to speak up?
How do you think Esther's heart felt in that moment?

back.transition: Let's see what the king does!

pshat.text: Mordechai told Esther about Haman's bad plan. Esther was scared, but she knew what she had to do. She went to the king and told him her secret!

guide.tip: Practice the deep breath together three times before the roleplay. It grounds the children.

cards.image_prompt:
ESTHER:
Young Jewish woman, warm olive skin, large kind brown eyes.
Long dark hair with elegant modest head covering.
Royal purple and blue flowing dress, simple gold tiara.
BEAMING with joy — the biggest smile, arms open wide!

MORDECHAI:
Older Jewish man, warm brown skin, kind wise eyes.
Full gray-brown beard. Jewish head covering.
Modest robes in earth tones. Clapping his hands with pride.

CELEBRATION! Esther and Mordechai together in center foreground.
Esther is dancing, her dress swirling. Mordechai claps beside her, eyes twinkling.
Behind them: a crowd of Jewish people CHEERING — hands raised, some playing tambourines and lutes.
Children in the foreground dancing and throwing confetti.
Colorful festive banners and streamers hang from Persian archways above.
Bright warm colors EVERYWHERE — golds, purples, reds, blues.
The whole scene BURSTS with energy and relief.
Festive canopy or palace ceiling visible above, decorated with flowers and garlands.
Dark festive ground at lower-left.

PURE JOY! This is the payoff — the danger is over, everyone is saved!
Let kids FEEL the celebration. Maximum energy, maximum happiness!

back.say: **When the king heard Esther's secret, he was so surprised! He loved Queen Esther. He stopped Haman's bad plan right away. The Jewish people were SAVED! Everyone was SO happy! They celebrated and danced and cheered! Let's celebrate too — jump up and down and cheer! YAY!** [Jump up and cheer! The Jewish people were saved!]

ask.text: How do you celebrate when something really good happens?
What made this story have a happy ending?

back.transition: What a wonderful ending! Now let's talk about it together.

pshat.text: The king listened to Esther. He stopped Haman's bad plan! All the Jewish people were saved, and everyone celebrated!

guide.tip: Let the celebration go for a full 10 seconds — children need to release the built-up tension.

cards.image_prompt:
Six diverse children (ages 4-6) sitting cross-legged in a circle on a round, colorful braided rug with concentric rings of red, blue, yellow, and green.

A girl with brown curly hair leans forward eagerly, one hand on her knee, mouth open mid-sentence — she is TELLING her story.
A boy in a striped kippah has his hand raised high, fingers spread, bouncing slightly — he wants to share next!
A boy with dark skin wearing a colorful knit kippah rests his chin on both hands, elbows on knees, listening with wide thoughtful eyes.
A girl with a pink headband sits with her arms wrapped around her knees, smiling shyly — warming up to speak.
Two more children sit attentively, one nodding, one with a hand on a friend's shoulder.

The classroom behind them feels LIVED-IN and warm:
A low wooden bookshelf with picture books and a teddy bear. Children's drawings taped to the wall (stick figures, a rainbow, a sun). A window with afternoon golden light streaming in, green trees visible outside. A small plant on the windowsill. Soft blue cubbies in the corner.

The rug is THEIR special circle-time spot — it feels familiar and safe.
Warm afternoon light fills the room. Hardwood floor around the rug.

COZY AND SAFE — like the best part of the school day, when everyone gets to share.

back.say: **Esther was really scared, but she was brave anyway. Let's sit in a circle and talk about being brave. Have YOU ever had to be brave, even when you were scared? Maybe speaking up, or trying something new? What helps you feel brave? Let's share with each other!**

ask.text: Have you ever had to be brave, even when you were scared?
How do you think Esther felt before she told her secret?

back.transition: You are all so brave for sharing!

guide.tip: Share your own brave moment first to model vulnerability. Children open up when adults go first.

cards.image_prompt:
Two children (ages 4-5) sitting together in a cozy reading nook in a classroom.

A boy wearing a knit kippah sits cross-legged, hugging a soft blue stuffed elephant to his chest. His eyes look upward and to the side — he is THINKING about something important. His expression is gentle, maybe a tiny bit worried, but mostly thoughtful. He wears a colorful striped button-up shirt and jeans.

Next to him, a girl with dark braids and a purple shirt sits with her knees pulled up, her chin resting on her arms. She LISTENS with kind, patient eyes — she is being a good friend. Her body leans slightly toward the boy, showing she cares.

They sit on big soft floor cushions in warm colors (orange, teal, mustard) arranged in a cozy nook. Behind them: a low bookshelf with colorful picture book spines visible, a soft knitted blanket draped over the shelf edge, a small potted plant. A window lets in warm golden afternoon light that makes everything glow. A children's drawing of a family is taped to the wall nearby.

The space feels like a SAFE CORNER — their special spot to talk about big feelings.
Warm, soft lighting. Gentle and protected.

TENDER AND SAFE — it's okay to have big feelings, especially with a friend nearby.

back.say: **Esther had to keep a big secret for a long time. That can feel hard! Have you ever had a secret that felt too big to hold inside? Sometimes we need to talk to a grown-up we trust. Who do you talk to when you have big feelings? Let's share in our circle.**

ask.text: Have you ever had a secret that was hard to keep?
How do you think Esther felt keeping her secret?

back.transition: Thank you for sharing your feelings with us!

guide.tip: If a child shares something sensitive, validate it warmly and follow up privately after circle time.

cards.image_prompt:
A warm, cozy synagogue community room decorated for Purim.
A friendly bearded man (generic community member, NOT a story character) stands in the center holding a megillah scroll open wide, reading aloud with an animated expression. The scroll faces TOWARD the reader — the viewer sees only the blank parchment back of the scroll, NOT the text side.
Adults sit in chairs in a semicircle around him — grandparents, parents, smiling and holding small megillah booklets.
Children sit cross-legged on the wooden floor in the foreground, grinning with excitement.
Several kids are shaking colorful groggers (noisemakers) — red, blue, green.
One boy covers his ears, laughing. A girl waves her grogger overhead.
Festive Purim decorations hang from the ceiling: paper streamers in blue, purple, gold.
Paper mask cutouts (crowns, stars) taped to the walls.
Warm pendant lights glow golden above. Warm wooden floor below.

Do NOT include Haman or any villain in this image. Show only positive, joyful community members.

Joyful community celebration! The fun of making noise TOGETHER!

back.say: **Remember how Haman made such a bad choice? Every year, when we read the Purim story and hear his name, we make LOTS of noise! We use a special noisemaker called a grogger. Can you say that? Gro-gger! It sounds like this —** [shake grogger] **. Let's practice! When I say 'Haman'... everyone shake! Ready? HAMAN!** [let kids shake] **Great job! That's how we celebrate Purim!**

ask.text: What is the loudest noise you can make?
Why do you think we make noise when we hear Haman's name?

back.transition: There are even more fun ways we celebrate Purim!

pshat.text: When someone reads the Purim story out loud, we listen carefully. Every time we hear 'Haman,' we shake our groggers as loud as we can!

guide.tip: If you don't have groggers, stomping feet and clapping hands works just as well.

cards.image_prompt:
A modern Jewish living room decorated for Purim. Warm, cozy, festive.
Four children showing off their Purim costumes to each other:
- A girl in a purple queen dress with a gold crown, holding a wand and twirling.
- A boy in a banana costume, laughing with his arms out.
- A younger boy as a red-caped superhero, hands on hips in a power pose.
- A girl in a colorful patchwork dress with a headband, giggling.
A plate of hamantaschen (triangle pastries) on a coffee table in the foreground.
Purim masks scattered on the table — a purple mask, a gold mask.
Festive streamers and balloons hanging from the ceiling.
A couch and lamp visible in the background. Warm golden living room light.

FUN, festive, IMAGINATIVE! Pure joy of playing dress-up. Kids should want to jump into this scene!

back.say: **Remember how Esther kept her Jewish identity hidden? It was like she was wearing an invisible costume! On Purim, we wear REAL costumes to remember Esther's secret. Some people dress as queens and kings. Some dress as animals or superheroes. Some wear silly costumes! If YOU could wear any Purim costume, what would you be? Let's share our ideas!**

ask.text: What would YOUR perfect Purim costume look like?
Why do you think dressing up is part of Purim?

back.transition: We have one more special Purim tradition to learn about!

pshat.text: On Purim, everyone wears costumes! We can dress up as queens, kings, heroes, or anything we want!

guide.tip: Have a few costume props ready (crown, cape, silly hat) to pass around while discussing.

cards.image_prompt:
A modern Jewish family kitchen — warm, bright, busy with Purim preparations.
A dad in a kippah arranging fruit in a wicker basket on the left side of the table.
A mom in a modest dress and apron placing hamantaschen (triangle pastries) on a tray.
A young boy in a kippah excitedly reaching into a basket, grabbing a wrapped candy.
A little girl in a striped dress holding up a plate of hamantaschen, proud of her work.
The kitchen table is covered with supplies: baskets, colorful cellophane wrap, ribbons, fruits, juice boxes, bags of treats.
Multiple gift baskets in various stages of being packed.
A window behind them shows green trees and warm sunlight.
A calendar and children's drawings on the kitchen wall.
Warm, bright kitchen lighting from above.

Generously warm, HOMEY, a real family doing something meaningful together. The joy of GIVING.

back.say: **When the Jewish people were saved, they were SO happy! They wanted to share that happy feeling with everyone. So they gave gifts of food to their friends and neighbors. On Purim, we do the same thing! We make baskets with treats and give them to people we care about. Who would YOU like to give a gift basket to?**

ask.text: Who would you most like to give a Purim gift to?
How does it feel when someone gives you a surprise gift?

back.transition: Purim is all about sharing joy with others!

pshat.text: On Purim, we make gift baskets filled with yummy treats. We give them to friends to spread happiness!

guide.tip: If possible, have the class make a simple mishloach manot together as a craft activity.

cards.image_prompt:
ESTHER:
Young Jewish woman, warm olive skin, large kind brown eyes.
Long dark hair with elegant modest head covering.
Royal purple and blue flowing dress with gold embroidery at the hem and cuffs.
Simple gold tiara catching the light. Delicate gold earrings.

Esther takes a brave step forward through a grand palace corridor.
Her right hand presses against her heart — steadying herself.
Her left hand is slightly extended forward, fingers spread, as if pushing through fear.
Her chin is lifted, jaw set with determination. Her eyes are focused and bright.
Her dress flows behind her with the motion of walking forward.

She walks FROM shadow INTO warm golden light — the glow of the throne room ahead.
Persian mosaic tile floor beneath her feet. Dark carved columns to either side at the edges.
The golden light ahead washes over her face and dress, making her glow.
Warm radiance fills the space above her — bright, open, luminous.

She looks SMALL against the tall corridor — but her posture says she is READY.
This is the bravest thing she has ever done.

PURE COURAGE! The moment a hero steps forward into the unknown.

back.say: **Let's learn a special Hebrew word: GIBOR. Can you say it? Gi-bor! It means 'hero' or 'brave one.' Esther was a gibor because she did the right thing even when she was scared. Guess what? YOU can be a gibor too! When you help someone, or try something new, or stand up for what's right — that's being a gibor. Let's all say it: 'I am a gibor!'**

ask.text: Who is a gibor in your life?
What is one brave thing you could do this week?

back.transition: Now you know an amazing Hebrew word!

pshat.text: A gibor is someone who does the right thing, even when it's hard or scary. YOU can be a gibor too!

guide.tip: Have children repeat 'I am a gibor!' three times, louder each time. End with a group cheer.
